# Realtime Lucy

`/apps/realtime-lucy` · Video · live · shows as: hub tile (`noPreview: true` — the carousel shows its animated icon, never a live frame)

> Your webcam, re-imagined live by a world model

A live video-to-video stream driven by LingBot-World 2.0's causal-fast world model, running on the
owner's own GPU. The webcam goes out over WebRTC; on the PC every quarter second of camera video is
encoded, noised into a four-step schedule, denoised against a rolling memory of what the model already
made, and streamed back. Type a prompt to change the look mid-stream, choose how much of the camera
to keep, hold WASD or the arrow keys to steer the model's own camera, and watch real numbers — it is
real model inference, not a filter.

![Realtime Lucy](../../public/look/realtime-lucy.jpg)

## Features — every one of these must still exist after your change

The owner asked for each of these. Removing, hiding or "simplifying away" one is a regression,
even if the code looked unused. If a change needs one gone, ask first.

**Start and stop** (`src/components/realtime-lucy/RealtimeLucy.tsx`)

- **One button: Start Lucy** — asks the studio bridge on this PC to start the GPU engine, watches the model load, and goes live by itself (becomes "Go live" if the server is already ready). `RealtimeLucy.tsx`, `src/lib/realtime-lucy/launcher.ts`, `tools/studio-bridge/server.mjs` (`/lucy/start`, `/lucy/status`)
- **Stop** (ends the stream) and **Stop the engine** — unloads the model and hands ~5.2 GB of VRAM back. `RealtimeLucy.tsx`, `launcher.ts` (`stopEngine`), bridge `/lucy/stop`
- **Honest status everywhere** — header dot + text (server online · GPU · model / model loading / starting / offline) and an explanation on the generated pane: engine off, model loading (20–30 s, first uncached prompt ~1 min more), "isn't installed on this PC yet", "Can't reach the launcher", or **"The launcher here is an older build"** (a bridge from before the Lucy routes — the page tells it apart and gives the stop-then-start commands). `RealtimeLucy.tsx`, `launcher.ts` (`BRIDGE_DOWN`, `BRIDGE_STALE`)
- **"What the button does" panel** — explains the bridge, shows `tools\studio-bridge\install-autostart.cmd` (plus `uninstall-autostart.cmd` first for an old build) and the last lines of the engine's log (`tools/studio-bridge/out/lucy.log`). `RealtimeLucy.tsx`

**The two screens**

- **Camera pane** — "Click to turn the camera on", then your live webcam. `RealtimeLucy.tsx`
- **Generated pane** — the model's frames over WebRTC, labelled "Generated · live"; a scan line while connecting; while a new prompt encodes it says the picture holds until it lands. `RealtimeLucy.tsx`, `src/lib/realtime-lucy/client.ts`

**Controls**

- **Prompt** — applies to the live stream on Enter (Shift+Enter = new line) or **Apply prompt**; label warns "edited, not applied — press Enter". `RealtimeLucy.tsx`
- **Six presets that apply on click** — cinematic room, oil painting, neon cyberpunk, hand-drawn anime, claymation, film noir. `src/lib/realtime-lucy/protocol.ts` (`PROMPT_PRESETS`)
- **How much of the camera to keep** — Faithful · Balanced · Dreamy · Free, with a one-line explanation each. `protocol.ts` (`STRENGTHS`)
- **Which part of the frame the prompt may repaint** — Whole frame · Background only · Me only; the region mode runs MediaPipe's selfie segmenter in the browser (CPU delegate, 4 times a second, sent as a 64-cell-wide grid) and says what % it is repainting, or falls back to unmasked if the segmenter fails. `src/lib/realtime-lucy/segmenter.ts`, `RealtimeLucy.tsx`; model files vendored in `public/mediapipe`
- **Drive the model's camera** — hold W/A/S/D, Q/E or the arrow keys while live; on-screen key caps light up. `RealtimeLucy.tsx` (`CAMERA_KEYS`)
- **Re-anchor** — forget the model's memory and restart from the current camera frame. `RealtimeLucy.tsx`
- **Connection settings** (hidden by default) — Lucy server URL (empty = go through this site's proxy), launcher URL (for a second PC with a big GPU), token, and conditioning mode SDEdit · Keyframe · Masked. Saved in localStorage. `RealtimeLucy.tsx`, `launcher.ts` (`LS_BRIDGE`)

**Live numbers**

- **Stats panel** — generated fps (and % of 16 fps), glass-to-glass latency, step time, denoise/stage timings, queue wait, peak VRAM, resolution, chunk, position, region locked %, camera frames, frames sent, plus a note on how latency is measured. `RealtimeLucy.tsx`

**On the PC** (`tools/realtime-lucy/`, not deployed)

- **GPU server** — aiohttp + aiortc WebRTC server running LingBot-World-V2's causal-fast path with SDEdit per chunk, rolling KV cache and streaming VAE; "masked" mode pastes the camera's own latents back outside the region after every denoising step, before the KV-cache write. Warms the six presets' text encodings while idle (cached on disk). Sends `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network` so an https page can reach localhost. `tools/realtime-lucy/server/server.py`, `server/common.py`, `lingbot/wan/streaming.py`
- **`start.ps1` picks a size that fits the card's VRAM** (288×384 on 6 GB spills to RAM and is ~8× slower). `tools/realtime-lucy/start.ps1`
- **Benchmarks** — `server/bench.py`, results in `tools/realtime-lucy/bench/RESULTS.md`.

## How it looks

- **Look:** DESIGN.md instrument panel unchanged, plus a hero glow; no design-skill record found.
- **Colours / type:** hub Tailwind tokens; cyan `text-accent` eyebrow "LINGBOT-WORLD 2.0 · CAUSAL-FAST · LIVE"; selected chips `border-brand bg-brand/15`. Status dot `#22c55e` (live) / `#f59e0b` (warming) / ink-faint (off). Key caps in mono, lit `--color-brand` when held. Video panes on `#000`. Stats values in mono.
- **Layout:** laptop — hero card, then camera and generated panes side by side (4:3 each), then controls (left) + 360 px "Live numbers" (right), then the help panel. Phone — every pair stacks.
- **Signature pieces:** the two framed panes with floating pill captions; WASD/arrow key caps over the generated pane; the stats definition list.
- **Motion:** only the scan line while connecting (`rl-scan` 2.4 s) and key-cap colour flips; no reduced-motion override exists for the scan line.

## Where the code is

| Page | `src/app/apps/realtime-lucy/page.tsx` |

| Logic + tests | `src/lib/realtime-lucy/` (`client.ts`, `protocol.ts`, `launcher.ts`, `segmenter.ts`) — tests live on the Python side (`tools/realtime-lucy/server/test_streaming.py`) |

# Music Video Studio

`/apps/seedance-studio` · Video · live · shows as: a panel on the Jarvis › Studio wall (one spine, "Engine"; clip `public/studio/music-video.mp4`). It is in `PLUGIN_SLUGS`, but `studioPlugins()` drops its App plugins card because `onTheWall()` is true (`src/lib/studio-home/panels.ts`), and it is off the hub grid. The slug keeps the old name "Seedance Studio"; the code folder is `seedance`.

> Audio-driven video engine

You drop a song and the film is cut to the song, not just laid over it. The browser measures the track (tempo, bar lines, sections, drops) and a listening model writes down the lyrics with their times. Then the same chat Jarvis Studio uses writes a shot plan where every cut is pinned to a second of the song. That plan becomes a three-lane timeline you can edit. You can render one cut at a time, or render the whole film free on the owner's GPU with the song on top as the master track.

![Music Video Studio](../../public/look/seedance-studio.jpg)

## Features — every one of these must still exist after your change

The owner asked for each of these. Removing, hiding or "simplifying away" one is a regression,
even if the code looked unused. If a change needs one gone, ask first.

**The track (measured in the browser, never uploaded)**
- **Drop a song and it is measured locally**: tempo, key, beat grid, bar lines, sections (intro/verse/build/chorus/bridge/outro guesses) and the loud hits and drops. Free and needs no key. `src/lib/seedance/audio/analyze.client.ts`, `src/lib/seedance/audio/grid.ts`, `src/lib/seedance/audio/timeline.ts`
- **Track strip pinned above the chat** shows what is known and how. MEASURED means tempo, bars and sections. HEARD means a model transcribed the words. PASTED means the owner's own lyrics were spread over the sung sections. It never mixes these up. `src/components/seedance/TrackStrip.tsx`
- **Transcribe the words with their times**: the song is cut into 40-second clips and each one goes to a listening model (Gemini via OpenRouter). The strip says the timings are close, not frame-accurate. If nothing is heard, it says the track may be instrumental. `src/lib/seedance/audio/transcribe.ts`, `src/app/api/seedance/transcribe/route.ts`
- **Paste lyrics** two ways: spread them evenly over the sung sections, or use the button "Use these words and let the model time them" (the model aligns your exact words). `src/components/seedance/TrackStrip.tsx`
- **Six visual modes**: Music video, Lyric video, Story, Voiceover, Reaction and Cinematic audio. The chosen mode goes to the director. `src/lib/seedance/audio/timeline.ts` (`VISUAL_MODES`), `src/components/seedance/TrackStrip.tsx`

**"The film" — the director chat (the only chat in the app)**
- **Same conversation as Jarvis Studio**: it posts to `/api/jarvis/chat` with the measured timeline, and the server adds the score rules (`scoreRules`). `src/components/seedance/SeedanceChat.tsx`, `src/app/api/jarvis/chat/route.ts`
- **@-mentions for workflows and people** from the Photos library (saved characters), **@Subject / @Audio** references to uploads, **#camera-move** autocomplete, and attachments by drag-drop or picker. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceChat.tsx`
- **Starter chips**: "Cut this to the drops", "Put the singer on camera through the chorus", "Make it night-time and neon", "Fewer, longer cuts". `src/components/seedance/SeedanceChat.tsx` (`STARTERS`)
- **Studio forms** the director can ask you to fill in, answered inside the chat. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceChat.tsx` (uses `../jarvis/StudioFormCard`)
- **Aspect ratio switch**: 16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceChat.tsx`, `src/lib/seedance/constants.ts`
- **Film-wide camera deck** (`CinemaBar`) under the composer. Every block inherits it. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceChat.tsx`, `src/lib/seedance/prompt.ts` (`mergedCinema`)
- **Local renderer status dot**: "Local renderer on · N queued" or "off", checked every 20 s. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceChat.tsx`

**The score (shot plan pinned to the song)**
- **Plan lands on the timeline**: each of the score's cuts becomes a video-prompt block, and its lip-sync ranges fill the lip-sync lane (`applyScore`). The plan's logline becomes the reel's direction. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceStudio.tsx`
- **Cuts snapped to measured bar lines and drops**. The director is told the exact bar times it may cut on, and a cut that misses its bar shows up as a "FIX" note. `src/lib/seedance/score.ts` (`scoreRules`, `scoreNotes`)
- **Lip sync outranks the prompt**: on a shot that sings, the woven prompt puts the performer on camera mouthing those exact words, and the visual idea becomes the world around them. `src/lib/seedance/score.ts` (`shotPrompt`)
- **Printed shot-plan sheet** (same format as Smart Shot Videos). It shows cut count, % of the track covered, and a shared-choices strip (aspect, lighting, lens, palette swatches + grade, world). Section 1 is cast and wardrobe. Section 2 is the song map and locations (sections, drops, every cut drawn on the track). Section 3 is the storyboard. Section 4 covers genre and treatment, style, story, logline, lighting and sound. Everything can be edited in place. `src/components/seedance/ScoreSheet.tsx`
- **Cut cards**: each shows its time on the track, lens | aperture | length | move | framing, an editable title/action/"because", and the sung words in italics. The card turns amber and shows a SINGS badge when that cut sings. `src/components/seedance/ScoreSheet.tsx` (`CutCard`)
- **Second board of just the singing cuts** ("Section 3B: Lip sync — N of M cuts"). `src/components/seedance/ScoreSheet.tsx`
- **Draw frames**: draw one cut's storyboard frame, or "Draw N frames" (three at a time). Frames are drawn from the whole plan, with the chat's reference faces. `src/components/seedance/ScoreSheet.tsx`, `src/lib/studio/panels.ts`
- **Render one cut before committing** (play button on a cut card). A rendered clip replaces that cut's frame. `src/components/seedance/ScoreSheet.tsx`, `src/components/seedance/SeedanceStudio.tsx` (`renderOne`)
- **The timeline wins**: the sheet always reads lip sync from the timeline (`liveScore`), so dragging a range changes which cuts sing everywhere. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceStudio.tsx`

**Make the film (free, on the owner's GPU)**
- **"Make the film"** renders every cut on the local studio bridge and lays the song over it as the master. The song plays at full level, unlooped, the clips' own audio is dropped, and each clip is trimmed back to its planned slot. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceChat.tsx` (`makeFilm`, `audioMode: "master"`), `src/lib/studio/film.ts`, `tools/studio-bridge/server.mjs`
- **Film progress with Cancel and Save .mp4**. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceChat.tsx` (uses `../jarvis/FilmProgress`)

**The cutting room — three lanes, always on screen**
- **Three lanes**: Video prompts (on top), Song with its real waveform (middle), Lip sync (bottom). The song lane has "Load the song" and a remove-song chip. The toolbar shows cut length, song length and lip-sync seconds. `src/components/seedance/Spine.tsx`, `src/components/seedance/SongBar.tsx`, `src/lib/seedance/client.ts` (`decodeSong`)
- **Zoom**: zoom in/out buttons, a log-scale zoom slider, and Fit. A zoom you picked yourself survives a window resize. `src/components/seedance/Spine.tsx`
- **Video prompt blocks**: add with "+" (at the end, or after any block), drag to reorder (neighbours slide closed), drag the right edge to trim (1–15 s, default 5 s), Delete key to remove. A block wears its first reference image as artwork until it has a rendered clip. `src/components/seedance/Blocks.tsx`, `src/lib/seedance/reel.ts`
- **Lip-sync ranges**: plain ranges with no prompt (1–30 s, default 5 s). Drag, trim, nudge with ←/→, delete, or click the lane to drop one at that second. Any block a range lands on turns amber and lip-syncs. `src/components/seedance/Blocks.tsx` (`LipRangeView`), `src/components/seedance/SeedanceStudio.tsx`
- **Prompt sheet** for a block: prompt text with #camera-move tokens (their order is the shot), the block's own camera deck rails (Film setup genre/era/tempo, Camera, Movement, Style, Color palette, Lighting) layered over the reel's, reference images, duration, and a collapsible "What Seedance reads" preview of the woven prompt. Buttons: Render this shot, Add the next prompt, Duplicate, Delete. `src/components/seedance/PromptSheet.tsx`, `src/lib/seedance/prompt.ts` (`composePrompt`), `src/lib/studio/cinema.ts`
- **Lip-sync sheet**: start/length steppers, how many shots it covers, Delete. `src/components/seedance/PromptSheet.tsx`
- **Stage**: the shot under the playhead (rendered clip, artwork, or a graded colour stand-in), Play/Pause, Rewind, "Open this shot's prompt", and a rendered-count. Selecting a block moves the playhead to it. `src/components/seedance/Stage.tsx`, `src/components/seedance/SeedanceStudio.tsx`
- **Shot list**: every prompt in order with its image, words and deck summary, plus a Render / done / failed cell per row. `src/components/seedance/ShotList.tsx`
- **Top rail**: Hub link, editable reel name, Save, "Render all N". Keys: Space plays/pauses, Esc closes the sheet. `src/components/seedance/SeedanceStudio.tsx`
- **Seedance 2 via the Vercel AI Gateway** for single blocks (image-to-video when the block has an image). Needs `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` (model `AI_VIDEO_MODEL`, default `bytedance/seedance-2.0`). Without the key, or if a render fails, it returns a graded colour placeholder so the editor still works offline. `src/app/api/seedance/route.ts`, `src/lib/seedance/client.ts`

## How it looks

- **Look:** the hub's Night Console (`DESIGN.md`) with the hub's own tokens: `bg-canvas`, `bg-panel`, `border-line`, `text-ink*`, and `accent` = `#00cae0` cyan (`src/app/globals.css`). No separate impeccable surface record.
- **Colours / type:** a strict three-colour rule (`src/lib/seedance/constants.ts`): **cyan** = the song and the playhead, **amber** (hue 36, text `hsl(40 96% 78%)`) = lip sync and any block it lands on, **indigo** (hue 246) = a block playing under the music. Hub system fonts and tiny uppercase lane labels (11px, 0.1em tracking), with tabular numbers for times. The score sheet reuses Smart Shot's paper sheet classes (`src/components/smart-shot/smart-shot.css`: Anton display, JetBrains Mono, paper `#f7f6f2`) plus `src/components/seedance/score-sheet.css`. Note that those `--ss-*` variables are declared on `.ss`, and this page does not wrap the sheet in `.ss`.
- **Layout:** laptop: a top rail, then Stage + "The film" chat side by side (capped at 420px tall), then the timeline, the score sheet and the shot list stacked below, with the prompt sheet docked as a 400px right column. Phone: everything stacks in one scrolling column, the "Render all" label shrinks to an icon, and the prompt sheet opens full screen.
- **Signature pieces:** the three-lane timeline with the waveform in the middle, amber lip-sync ranges lining up with amber blocks, blocks that show their reference image like a storyboard, and the paper shot-plan sheet with its song map.
- **Motion:** blocks slide closed after a drag (`.sd-slide`), a light sweep crosses a block while it renders (`.sd-render`), the sheet slides in (`.sd-sheet`), and a sheen moves on the film progress bar. With `prefers-reduced-motion` all of these are off (`src/app/globals.css`).

## Where the code is

| Part | Path |
|---|---|
| Page | `src/app/apps/seedance-studio/page.tsx` |
| UI | `src/components/seedance/` (shell `SeedanceStudio.tsx`) |
| Logic + tests | `src/lib/seedance/` (`reel.ts`, `score.ts`, `prompt.ts`, `audio/*`; tests `reel.test.ts`, `score.test.ts`, `audio/grid.test.ts`, `audio/transcribe.test.ts`) |
| API | `src/app/api/seedance/` (`route.ts` = one clip, `transcribe/route.ts` = lyrics); the director is `src/app/api/jarvis/chat/route.ts` |
| Saved data | synced key `seedance-studio:v3` (reels, structure only: no song, refs or clips; `src/lib/seedance/repo.ts`) · synced key `seedance-chat:v1` (the conversation + visual mode; `SeedanceChat.tsx`). The score itself is not saved; it lives in this session only. |

Also used: the shared Studio pieces in `src/components/jarvis/` (CinemaDeck, MentionMenu, StudioFormCard, FilmProgress, ReferenceTile) and `src/lib/studio/` (cinema, film, render, storyboard, panels). The film render is the PC bridge in `tools/studio-bridge/`. Env keys: `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, `AI_VIDEO_MODEL`, `SEEDANCE_LISTEN_MODEL` / `MUSIC_LISTEN_MODEL`, and OpenRouter for transcription.

## Owner's rules for this app

- The song is the master. Cuts land on measured bar lines and drops, and a clip that comes back longer than its slot is trimmed, never allowed to push later cuts out of sync (`score.ts` header).
- Lip sync outranks the prompt. On a singing cut the performer and the words are the subject, and the idea becomes the world around them.
- Only three lanes, and prompts live only in video blocks. The lip-sync lane never carries a prompt (feature log, 23 Sep 2026).
- The colour rule never changes: cyan = song, amber = lip sync, indigo = plays under the music.
- There is exactly one chat in this app ("The film"). Never add a second director box.
- The song never leaves the browser. Only its measurements (and 40-second clips, if transcription is asked for) are sent. Lyric timings are approximate, and the UI must say so.
- The timeline is the source of truth for lip sync. The sheet and the film read it from there.
- Save structure only, never the heavy media (song, reference images and clips are session-only).

## Described but not found in code

- "Move a cut, split it, lock it, toggle whether it sings" and "Snap to bars" — catalog overview. The code exists in `src/components/seedance/ScoreBoard.tsx` (views All / Sings / Both, split, lock, sing toggle, snap), but nothing imports that file, so none of it is on screen. The mounted `ScoreSheet.tsx` only edits text in place and changes singing through the lip-sync lane.
- "Rewrite the woven prompt" — catalog overview. The mounted UI shows the woven prompt read-only ("What Seedance reads" in `PromptSheet.tsx`). You can edit a cut's action/title, but there is no field to rewrite the woven prompt itself.
- "The original three-lane cutting room is still there behind a toggle" — catalog overview. There is no toggle: the three-lane timeline (`Spine.tsx`) is always shown, with the score sheet below it.

# Skills Library

`/apps/skills-library` · — (no catalog entry) · live · shows as: Toolbox tab (Jarvis › More › Toolbox › **Skills**, `/apps/jarvis#skills`)

> (No catalog tag line — Skills Library is not in `src/lib/catalog.ts` `PROJECTS`. The page heading reads "My Skills": "Your Claude Code skills, synced and searchable by name, nickname or category.")

The owner's library of every skill they have — their own Claude Code skills, plugin skills, the
Studio agents and a few built-in ones — in one searchable list. It shows how to call each skill,
its nicknames and categories, how often it gets called, and what it costs, and lets the owner cap a
skill's weekly spend or fix which model it runs on. It used to be its own app; since 2026-09-21 it
is a tab inside Jarvis, and the old route just redirects there.

![Skills Library](../../public/look/skills-library.jpg)

## Features — every one of these must still exist after your change

The owner asked for each of these. Removing, hiding or "simplifying away" one is a regression,
even if the code looked unused. If a change needs one gone, ask first.

**Where it lives**

- **A tab in Jarvis's Toolbox** — Toolbox › Skills mounts the library with no Hub bar (`chromeless`). `src/components/new-jarvis/NewJarvis.tsx` (tab `skills`, `<SkillsLibrary chromeless />`)
- **Old link still works** — `/apps/skills-library` redirects to `/apps/jarvis#skills`. `src/app/apps/skills-library/page.tsx`
- **"Skills on every device" card** — above the list, shows whether skill sync is set up on this device and the next step. `src/components/jarvis/SyncStatusPanel.tsx` (mounted in `NewJarvis.tsx`)

**Where the skills come from**

- **Auto-sync on open + Sync button** — opening the library re-reads every skill source; the Sync button does it on demand and says how many synced. `src/components/skills/SkillsLibrary.tsx` (`runSync`) → `src/lib/skills/store.ts` `syncFromClaudeCode` → `src/app/api/skills/scan/route.ts`
- **Five sources merged, newest copy wins** — committed project pack `.claude/skills/`, the repo mirror `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, Jarvis's skill store (Supabase `jarvis_memories` rows with `source = "skill"`, written by the connector's `save_skill` and by `skill-sync.mjs`), the live `~/.claude/skills/` on this machine, and installed plugin skills under `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`. Precedence lowest→highest: pack, repo, store, personal, plugins. `src/app/api/skills/scan/route.ts`
- **Works when deployed** — personal SKILL.md files are mirrored into `skills/` so the hosted site shows the same skills as the PC (change log 2026-09-24). `src/app/api/skills/scan/route.ts` (`scanRepo`)
- **Studio agents appear as skills** — every Studio workflow's skill file is served as a library record. `src/app/api/skills/studio/route.ts`, loaded by `src/lib/skills/store.ts` (`studioSkills`)
- **Built-in "featured" skills** — read-only skills that ship with the app (e.g. `github:scroll-world`); a synced or hand-added skill with the same slug/title replaces it. `src/lib/skills/seed-skills.ts`, `src/lib/skills/store.ts` (`withFeatured`)
- **Screenshot of a prompt → a skill** — a photo of a prompt filed from the Dashboard photo inbox becomes a Skills Library record, transcribed word for word. `src/lib/dashboard/destinations/skillsLibrary.ts` (registered in `src/lib/dashboard/destinations/registry.ts`)

**Finding a skill**

- **All skills / ★ Favorites switch** — starred skills in one folder; stars sync across devices (key `skills-favorites:v1`, keyed by slug so a re-sync keeps the star). `src/components/skills/SkillsLibrary.tsx`, `src/lib/skills/favorites.ts`
- **Search by name, nickname or category.** `src/lib/skills/categories.ts` (`matchesQuery`)
- **Category bar, always on screen** — pinned while you scroll, lists all 19 standard categories with counts (empty ones shown dimmed so chips never move). `src/components/skills/SkillsLibrary.tsx`, `src/lib/skills/categories.ts` (`CATEGORY_ORDER`, `categoriesIn`)
- **Web Design tagging from the design roster** — every skill in `src/lib/redesigner/design-skills.json` is tagged Web Design (the roster is appended to by `scripts/sync-design-skills.mjs`). `src/lib/skills/categories.ts`
- **Source filter** — All / Personal / each plugin name, Personal first. `src/components/skills/SkillsLibrary.tsx` (`origins`)
- **Sort row** — Recommended, Most used, Most spend, Newest, Oldest, Recently updated, A–Z. `src/lib/skills/sort.ts` (`SORTS`, `sortSkills`)
- **"Added" window** — Any time, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This year. `src/lib/skills/sort.ts` (`ADDED`, `addedWithin`)
- **Sort, Added and Usage choices remembered per browser** (localStorage `skills-library:sort:v1`). `src/components/skills/SkillsLibrary.tsx` (`readView`/`pickView`)
- **Usage filter** — Any · Top 10 · Used · Never used · Retire? (never called, or idle 45+ days), each with its count. `src/lib/skills/usage.ts` (`USAGE_FILTERS`, `RETIRE_DAYS`), `src/lib/skills/spend.ts` (`retireCandidates`)
- **Nickname clash warning** — an amber banner when two skills answer to the same nickname. `src/lib/skills/categories.ts` (`nicknameClashes`), shown in `SkillsLibrary.tsx`

**Each skill row**

- **Name, source badge, categories, up to 4 nicknames, "Added <date>"**. `src/components/skills/SkillRow.tsx` (`OriginBadge`, `addedLabel` from `src/lib/skills/sort.ts`)
- **Usage badge** — "N calls · used X ago", #1–#3 most-used lit (rank is among all skills, whatever filter is on). `src/components/skills/SkillRow.tsx` (`UsageBadge`), `src/lib/skills/usage.ts`
- **Spend badge** — this week's cost/tokens (hover: lifetime cost and runs), amber at 80% of its cap, red when over. `src/components/skills/SkillRow.tsx` (`SpendBadge`)
- **Star, edit, delete** from the row. `src/components/skills/SkillRow.tsx`

**Skill detail and editing**

- **Detail window** — how to call it (`/name`) and its nicknames (or a hint to add "Nicknames: …" to the description), the full markdown prompt, **Copy prompt**, **View on GitHub** when it has a source link, star, Edit, Delete. `src/components/skills/SkillDetailModal.tsx`
- **Weekly dollar cap + model pin per skill** — set a weekly $ cap (over it the skill runs on the free model "till Monday") and pin a tier (Free / Cheap / Best model) or leave it to Jev. `src/components/skills/SkillDetailModal.tsx` → `PATCH /api/skills/spend` (needs sign-in) `src/app/api/skills/spend/route.ts`
- **Add a skill by pasting markdown** — title and overview fill themselves from the frontmatter as you paste. `src/components/skills/SkillEditorModal.tsx`, `src/lib/skills/parse.ts`
- **Editing a built-in makes your own copy** that takes its place; deleting that copy brings the built-in back (worded as "Discard your edits"). `src/lib/skills/store.ts` (`forkSkill`, `isBuiltIn`), `src/components/skills/SkillsLibrary.tsx` (`handleSave`, `handleDelete`)
- **Delete with confirm** ("This can't be undone"). `src/components/skills/SkillsLibrary.tsx`
- **Web design guide dropdown** — collapsible "which web design skill?" list: one paragraph + "best for" per skill, a Yours / Anthropic / Added badge, Open (if in the library) or a GitHub link. `src/components/skills/DesignGuide.tsx`, `src/lib/skills/design-guide.ts`

**Usage counting (how the call counts are made)**

- **Counts every skill call** — Claude Code on the PC/VPS (Skill tool + typed `/<skill>`, via the silent `skill-sync.mjs usage` hook → `/api/jarvis/skills/usage`, token; `pull` installs the hooks and backfills past calls once per machine), the connector's `get_skill` (`src/app/api/jarvis/memory/mcp/route.ts`), and Jarvis Studio workflow runs in `src/app/api/jarvis/chat/route.ts` (keys `studio:<id>`). Stored in one `app_state` row `jarvis:skill-usage`, no migration. `src/lib/skills/server/usageStore.ts`, `scripts/skill-sync.mjs`
- **Matching a call to a skill** — keys are call names (`felix`, `superpowers:brainstorming`, `studio:<id>`); `usageFor` matches by slug, then bare plugin name, then title. `src/lib/skills/usage.ts`
- **Updates by itself** — the page re-reads counts every minute. `src/lib/skills/useSkillUsage.ts` (`REFRESH_MS = 60_000`) → `src/app/api/skills/usage/route.ts`
- **Usage summary line** — "N calls across X of Y skills — from Claude Code on your computers, the Jarvis connector and Studio." `src/components/skills/SkillsLibrary.tsx`

**Spend and Jev model routing**

- **Weekly spend line** — this week's $ and tokens across skills, how many are over cap, and what Jev routed (runs, average ms, cost, runs sent to a cheaper model). `src/components/skills/SkillsLibrary.tsx` (`spendTotals`), `src/lib/skills/useSkillSpend.ts`
- **Jarvis runs are metered** — `recordCall` adds a call's cost to the skill when the call's `task.skill` is set (Jarvis Studio runs set it). `src/lib/ai/spend.ts` → global doc `skill-spend` next to `ai-spend`, writes batched. `src/lib/skills/server/spendStore.ts`
- **Claude Code runs are metered (estimates)** — Stop hook `skill-sync.mjs usage-cost` reads only new transcript lines and posts tokens per skill to `/api/jarvis/skills/usage` (`spend`), priced from the model catalogue at API rates. `scripts/skill-sync.mjs`, `src/lib/skills/server/priceTokens.ts`
- **Jev picks free/cheap/best per skill run** — `provider.ts` `planCall` → `routeSkill` (1.5 s ceiling; only when the router is choosing). Tier order: pin › cap › Jev › router. `src/lib/ai/provider.ts`, `src/lib/skills/server/routeSkill.ts`, `src/lib/skills/spend.ts` (`chooseTier`, `addSpend`, `capState`, `bySpend`, `retireCandidates`)

**Storage**

- **Per-user cloud storage with a local fallback** — Supabase `skills` table with per-user RLS when configured; otherwise localStorage, and the stand-alone header shows a "Local mode" badge. `src/lib/skills/store.ts` (`isCloudBacked`), `supabase/migrations/20260831000200_skills_library.sql`

## How it looks

- **Look:** the hub's standard "Night Console" dark app chrome (see `DESIGN.md`); no app-specific design skill recorded.
- **Colours / type:** hub tokens only — `bg-canvas` `#0a0b0f`, `bg-panel` `#12141c`, `bg-panel-2` `#181b25`, borders `line` `#262a38`, text `ink` `#e9ecf3` / `ink-muted` `#9aa3b5` / `ink-faint` `#6b7385`, accent `brand` `#6366f1` (active chips `bg-brand/15 text-brand`, primary button `bg-brand`, hover `brand-2` `#4f46e5`). Success text `core` `#22c55e`; amber for the nickname-clash banner, red for errors and over-cap. System sans for text, JetBrains Mono for counts and badges.
- **Layout:** one centred column (`max-w-3xl`) on a laptop: heading, All/Favorites segmented switch, search + Sync + Add skill, then filter rows (Category, Source, Sort, Added, Usage), the spend line, the Web design guide, and the skill rows stacked as rounded cards. On a phone the same column; filter rows scroll sideways instead of wrapping, and the Sync/Add buttons drop their labels to icons. Inside Jarvis the Hub bar is hidden.
- **Signature pieces:** the sticky blurred Category chip bar (`bg-canvas/95 backdrop-blur`), pill-shaped filter chips (dimmed when empty), the "N calls · used X ago" usage badge with #1–#3 lit, the spend badge, the amber nickname-clash banner.

## Where the code is

| Part | Path |
|---|---|
| Page | `src/app/apps/skills-library/page.tsx` (redirect to `/apps/jarvis#skills`); mounted in `src/components/new-jarvis/NewJarvis.tsx` |

# Smart Shot Videos

`/apps/smart-shot-videos` · Video · live · shows as: hub tile

> Prompt → editable storyboard → H3 video

A recreation of OpenArt's Smart Shot inside the hub. The owner writes one paragraph about a short film or ad, adds reference photos, and gets a full production sheet with character sheets, set plates, a floor plan, one storyboard frame per cut and lighting references. Everything on the sheet can be edited or redrawn. When the sheet looks right, MiniMax H3 renders the whole film as one video.

![Smart Shot Videos](../../public/look/smart-shot-videos.jpg)

## Features — every one of these must still exist after your change

The owner asked for each of these. Removing, hiding or "simplifying away" one is a regression,
even if the code looked unused. If a change needs one gone, ask first.

**The app around the sheet**
- **Three-step header**: 1 Prompt + images · 2 Editable shot plan · 3 H3 video. Steps 2 and 3 stay locked until a plan exists. `src/components/smart-shot/SmartShot.tsx`
- **Projects**: a picker in the header (up to 20 saved, newest first), "+ New project", and delete with a confirm prompt. `src/components/smart-shot/SmartShot.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/repo.ts`
- **Picks up where you left off**: renders still running when the page closed keep checking when it reopens. A panel or take cut off halfway is cleaned up on load. `src/components/smart-shot/studio.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/repo.ts`
- **Error and notice banner** with a dismiss button. Examples: "planned locally", or a planner failure that fell back to the offline planner. `src/components/smart-shot/SmartShot.tsx`

**Step 1 — Prompt + images**
- **Scene box with three example prompts**: chocolate commercial, summer drink, girl on a bicycle. `src/components/smart-shot/Brief.tsx`
- **Tagged references, up to 9 (H3's limit)**. Three drop zones: Characters & objects, Environment, Style. Each image can be re-tagged Character / Environment / Product-object / Style, given a name and a note, or removed. `src/components/smart-shot/Brief.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/constants.ts`
- **Every way in**: click to pick, drag a file, drag an image from another page, paste a screenshot (Ctrl+V on a focused box), or paste an image link. iPhone HEIC photos are converted, and images are shrunk to 1024 px. `src/components/smart-shot/Brief.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/media.ts`
- **Shoot settings**: Cuts 3/4/5/6 · Length 6/10/15 s · Aspect 16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1 · Quality Medium 768p / High 2K · Look (Live-action film, Commercial, Documentary, Anime, 3D animation). A summary line shows seconds per cut and an estimated cost. `src/components/smart-shot/Brief.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/constants.ts`
- **Two buttons**: "Preview shot plan" plans the film and draws the sheet. "Create video" plans, draws and renders the film in one go. `src/components/smart-shot/Brief.tsx`, `src/components/smart-shot/studio.tsx`
- **The planner looks at your photos**, so a character drawn from a photo is described as that person. With no AI key, or when the model fails, an offline planner builds the sheet instead, so a sheet always comes back. `src/app/api/smart-shot/plan/route.ts`, `src/lib/smart-shot/plan/heuristic.ts`, `src/lib/smart-shot/plan/prompt.ts`, `src/lib/smart-shot/plan/schema.ts`

**Step 2 — the shot-plan sheet** (paper-white, in OpenArt's layout)
- **Shared choices strip**: cut count, aspect, a Lighting label, a Lens label, the palette as colour swatches plus a note, and an "environment fingerprint" (one line that pins down the setting). All editable. `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`
- **Section 1, character reference**: a six-panel turnaround for each character (front, three-quarter and back views, two portraits, a wardrobe close-up) drawn from the uploaded photo, with palette swatches and editable Look and Wardrobe text. `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/panels.ts`
- **Section 1, product / hero object**: a product sheet labelled with five views (front, three-quarter, side/edge, macro detail, in context), palette swatches, an editable description and notes you can add. The heading changes to Character / Character + Product / Product to match. `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/panels.ts`
- **Section 2, set design**: a picture of each location, editable Set Notes and Props, and a top-down floor plan with a numbered camera marker for every cut. The legend lists each cut and its camera move. `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/panels.ts`
- **Side elevation** of the last cut's camera path (for example a crane move), drawn as three heights. `src/lib/smart-shot/panels.ts`, `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`
- **Section 3, storyboard**: one frame per cut, captioned with lens (mm), aperture, seconds, move, framing and angle. Each frame is drawn from that cut's character sheets and set plate so faces and places match. `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`, `src/components/smart-shot/studio.tsx`
- **Cut editing**: move a cut earlier or later, add a cut (8 at most), or delete one (at least 1 stays). The pencil opens lens, aperture, move (14 kinds), framing, angle, seconds, set, who is in the shot, action, dialogue (H3 lip-syncs it) and where it sits on the floor plan. `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/constants.ts`
- **Section 4, lighting, mood and style**: always four lighting reference pictures, each tied to a real light source in the scene, with editable captions. Also mood keywords, a one-line style essence, cinematography notes, and Sound (ambience + music). `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/plan/schema.ts`
- **Edit any word in place**: click any text on the sheet, then click away or press Enter to save. `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx` (`Editable`)
- **Redraw any picture**: each panel has a "Recreate image" / "Draw" button that redraws it from the current text. A toolbar button draws any missing panels, and a status shows how many are still drawing. Panels made with no image key are marked "offline preview". `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`, `src/app/api/smart-shot/panel/route.ts`, `src/lib/smart-shot/placeholder.ts`

- **Download the sheet** as a single JPG made from every panel. The same image is attached to the film render. `src/lib/smart-shot/sheetImage.ts`, `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`
- **AI director chat**, docked beside the sheet. Say what to change, or tap a starter ("Make it night-time with moonlight"…). The whole plan is rewritten, and only the panels whose content changed are redrawn. With no AI key it says so and points you to hand editing. `src/components/smart-shot/DirectorChat.tsx`, `src/app/api/smart-shot/revise/route.ts`, `src/lib/smart-shot/plan/revise.ts`
- **Next-step bar**: "Edit with AI" (puts the cursor in the chat), "Create video", and "View last video" once a film exists. `src/components/smart-shot/Sheet.tsx`

**Step 3 — H3 video**
- **One H3 generation for the whole film**: one compiled prompt with a [Shot N] block per cut. The character and product sheets, set plates, the composed sheet and one style image go in as references, and the length is capped at 4–15 s. `src/lib/smart-shot/h3prompt.ts` (`composeFullH3Prompt`), `src/components/smart-shot/studio.tsx`
- **H3 brief in H3's reference format**: subject_definitions, summary, retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape and non_diegetic_music. Camera moves are written as sentences with an amplitude and a speed. Lens and depth of field are written as words, and the angle is named unless it is eye-level. Dialogue gets speaker ids. At most 9 images. `src/lib/smart-shot/h3prompt.ts`
- **Player + Download MP4**, plus a "Shot plan" download, "Recreate video", and a take picker once there are several films. `src/components/smart-shot/VideoStage.tsx`
- **Which video service is on**: shows the active backend and the cost estimate. With no backend it says which keys to add and renders a stand-in animatic. Renders go through `/api/auteur/generate`, which picks your own H3 on RunPod, MiniMax hosted, the AI Gateway, or the stand-in. `src/components/smart-shot/VideoStage.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/client.ts`, `src/lib/auteur/server/video/index.ts`
- **Advanced, folded away**: the full H3 prompt, which can be copied, edited by hand, saved or reset. Each cut also has its own H3 prompt (same edit/reset), its own render (at least 4 s, with its storyboard frame attached), retakes and an mp4 download. `src/components/smart-shot/VideoStage.tsx`, `src/lib/smart-shot/h3prompt.ts` (`composeH3Prompt`)

## How it looks

- **Look:** "a dark studio around a paper-white sheet": a black workspace with a printed production document in the middle. Its own look, scoped under `.ss`. It does not use DESIGN.md's Night Console tokens. No design-skill record in `.impeccable/`.

Paper `--ss-paper #f7f6f2` / `#ecebe5`, paper lines `#cfcdc4`, paper ink `#1b1b1b` / `#4a4a48`. Primary buttons and the "VIDEOS" in the wordmark are indigo `--ss-brand #6366f1`. Errors red `#e5533d`, OK green `#5fc98a`. Type: the condensed display stack "Anton", Oswald, Bebas Neue, Impact for the wordmark and section titles. JetBrains Mono for labels, specs and prompts. "Inter"/system-ui on the sheet. Georgia italic for mood words. Anton and Inter are not loaded by the app, so the display falls back to an installed font such as Impact.

# Tap Safe

`/apps/std-safe` · Apps · live · shows as: hub tile

> Provable results, honest about what they don't prove

A tracker for the STD lab reports a person already gets, and a way to show someone else what they were tested for, what came back, and how old each sample is. You upload the lab PDF (or a photo), check every line on a review screen, and then share your card in person with a six-character code. The app never says "clean" and always shows what a result cannot prove. The slug, routes and storage keep the old name "STD Safe" so existing reports and share codes still work. The code folder is `stdsafe`.

![Tap Safe](../../public/look/std-safe.jpg)

## Features — every one of these must still exist after your change

The owner asked for each of these. Removing, hiding or "simplifying away" one is a regression,
even if the code looked unused. If a change needs one gone, ask first.

**Account**

- **Own sign-up / sign-in** — handle (3–24 chars) + password + display name. This is separate from the hub login. Before it asks for anything, the screen shows three promises ("Reads the report you already have", "Never says the word clean", "Nobody sees anything without a yes"). `src/components/stdsafe/AuthPanel.tsx`, `src/app/api/std-safe/auth/route.ts`, `src/lib/stdsafe/store.ts`
- **Short session** — HMAC-signed cookie `stdsafe_session`, 14 days. Deleting a user revokes it. There is no admin role on purpose. `src/lib/stdsafe/session.ts`
- **Sign out** — in the top bar, with your @handle beside it. `src/components/stdsafe/StdSafe.tsx`

**Adding results**

- **Drop a lab report** — drag and drop or click to add a PDF or image, up to 20MB. It accepts reports from STDcheck, Quest, Labcorp and MyChart, and is read on the server. `src/components/stdsafe/UploadFlow.tsx`, `src/app/api/std-safe/parse/route.ts`
- **Careful PDF reader** — cuts off the reference range before reading the result, so "Non Reactive" in the range is never mistaken for the answer. Lines it cannot read go into an "ambiguous" list instead of being guessed. `src/lib/stdsafe/parse.ts`
- **AI help, optional** — a vision model reads a phone photo or screenshot. A text model takes a second pass when the PDF reader comes back thin. With no key, it says so and falls back to typing it in by hand. `src/lib/stdsafe/ai.ts`
- **Enter by hand** — "No file — enter the results by hand", given the same weight as uploading and saved as self-reported. `src/components/stdsafe/UploadFlow.tsx`
- **Review screen before anything is saved** — lab, panel, collection date (required) and reported date. All ten infections get a row (HIV, syphilis, chlamydia, gonorrhea, hep B, hep C, HSV-1, HSV-2, trich, M. gen), each defaulting to "Not tested" with Negative / Positive / Inconclusive. Lines it could not read are printed word for word. It is labelled LAB DOCUMENT or SELF-REPORTED, and nothing saves without at least one test marked. `src/components/stdsafe/DraftReview.tsx`, `src/lib/stdsafe/types.ts`
- **Treatment context on positives** — Treated & cleared, In treatment, Managed — undetectable, On suppressive therapy, Not yet treated. `CONTEXT_LABELS` in `src/lib/stdsafe/types.ts`, chosen in `src/components/stdsafe/DraftReview.tsx`

**Your card (status)**

- **Status per infection, not per record** — every row has its own sample date and age ("12 days ago"). Freshness is fresh up to 30 days, aging up to 90, stale after that. `src/lib/stdsafe/status.ts`, `src/components/stdsafe/StatusCard.tsx`
- **Untested rows stay visible in grey** — "X of 10 tested" and "Not covered: …" sit in the card, so a two-test panel never looks like a full workup. `src/components/stdsafe/StatusCard.tsx`
- **Positives handled fairly** — a managed positive (for example undetectable) shows amber, not red. An untreated positive shows red. `rowTone` in `src/components/stdsafe/StatusCard.tsx`
- **Evidence chips** — LAB DOC or SELF on each row, and a footer saying whether every result, some results or none are backed by a document. `VerificationChip` in `src/components/stdsafe/StatusCard.tsx`
- **"What this does not tell you"** — three standing caveats on every card and in the side panel: a result only covers exposure before the sample date; a file on record proves a document exists, not that it is authentic; window periods vary. `STANDING_CAVEATS` in `src/lib/stdsafe/status.ts`

**Records**

- **Records timeline** — every record, newest first, with its note, a "View document" link to the attached file (served only to its owner), and Delete with a "Delete for good" confirm. `src/components/stdsafe/RecordTimeline.tsx`, `src/app/api/std-safe/records/route.ts`, `src/app/api/std-safe/report/route.ts`, `src/lib/stdsafe/reports.ts`

**Sharing (in-person handshake)**

- **Your code** — a six-character code with no I/1/O/0, shown large in monospace, with a Copy button. `CodeChip` in `src/components/stdsafe/StdSafe.tsx`, code made in `src/lib/stdsafe/store.ts`
- **Rotate code** — gives you a new code and cuts off everyone who can currently see your card, after a confirm. `CodeChip` in `src/components/stdsafe/StdSafe.tsx`, `src/app/api/std-safe/me/route.ts`
- **Ask someone** — type their six characters. Input is upper-cased and stripped as you type. `src/components/stdsafe/AskPanel.tsx`, `src/app/api/std-safe/requests/route.ts`
- **Requests inbox** — "Asking you": "Preview what they'd see" (the exact same card component), Deny, Approve. An approval opens your card for 24 hours, with a countdown and Revoke. "You asked": View, once approved. `src/components/stdsafe/RequestInbox.tsx`, grant rules in `src/lib/stdsafe/store.ts` (`GRANT_TTL_MS`)
- **Silent denials** — a denied request simply stops appearing for the asker. A refusal never shows up as a refusal. `src/components/stdsafe/RequestInbox.tsx`
- **Shared view overlay** — the other person's card plus "Where this came from" (date, lab, panel, document or self-reported) and the expiry time. Report files are never shared. `ViewOverlay` in `src/components/stdsafe/StdSafe.tsx`, `src/app/api/std-safe/view/route.ts`
- **Live prompts while standing together** — the dashboard polls every 6 s. An amber banner ("Someone is asking to see your card · Answer →") and a count on the Requests tab show what is waiting. `src/components/stdsafe/StdSafe.tsx`

**Honesty about storage**

- **"Nothing here will be kept." banner** — shown when the server cannot store data permanently. `src/components/stdsafe/StdSafe.tsx`, `src/lib/stdsafe/store.ts`

## How it looks

- **Look:** the hub's DESIGN.md "near-black instrument panel", used unchanged (Tailwind tokens `bg-canvas`, `bg-panel`, `border-line`, `text-ink`/`ink-muted`/`ink-faint`, `bg-brand`, `support`). No design skill is recorded for it.
- **Colours / type:** colour only marks state. Emerald for negative and fresh, amber for aging, inconclusive, managed positives and pending requests, rose for untreated positives, stale and errors, grey at 55% opacity for untested rows. `support` blue is the LAB DOC chip. The share code is in monospace at 3xl with wide tracking. Row dates are in mono 11px. The brand mark is an emerald dot plus "Tap Safe".
- **Layout:** sticky top bar ("← Hub" | ● Tap Safe | @handle, Sign out). On a laptop: max-w-6xl, a two-column grid (`lg:grid-cols-[1fr_320px]`) with the tabs (Your card / Records / Requests) on the left and the code chip and "Always true" caveats on the right. On a phone: one column with the code chip first. Row dates and evidence chips are hidden below `sm`. The sign-in page is a two-column hero with a form.
- **Signature pieces:** `StatusCard.tsx` (one component for your view, the approval preview and the shared view), the big code chip, the amber "asking" banner.
- **Motion:** almost none. Colour transitions on hover, and `animate-fade-in` on the preview and shared overlay.

## Where the code is

| Part | Path |
|---|---|
| Page | `src/app/apps/std-safe/page.tsx` |
| UI | `src/components/stdsafe/` |
| Logic + tests | `src/lib/stdsafe/` |
| API | `src/app/api/std-safe/` (`auth`, `me`, `parse`, `records`, `report`, `requests`, `view`) |
| Saved data | server_docs doc `.std-safe.json` (locally a file under `STDSAFE_DATA_DIR` or the working dir); report files in the private Supabase Storage bucket `std-safe-reports` (`std-safe-reports/<user>/<file>`, migration `supabase/migrations/20260905000300_std_safe_reports_bucket.sql`) |

## Owner's rules for this app

- The app is called **Tap Safe**, but the slug `std-safe`, the routes and the Supabase bucket keep the old name so existing reports and share codes survive. Do not rename them.
- The word **"clean" appears nowhere**, and there is no "clean" field in the data model.
- Status is per infection, never one overall date. Untested infections are always shown, never left out.
- Positives carry treatment context. An undetectable/managed positive is not shown as a red alarm.
- Nothing parsed is saved until the person confirms every line.
- Sharing is a live handshake: a code, a preview, an approval for 24 hours. Denials are silent, and rotating the code cuts everyone off.
- Report files (legal name, date of birth) are never shared. Only the owner's session can reach them.
- Every result page carries the two things it cannot prove: that the document is real, and that nothing has happened since the sample.
- Every rule is enforced on the server (`store.ts`), never only in the UI.

## Described but not found in code

- None found.

# Text Inbox

`/apps/text-inbox` · AI · live · shows as: Dashboard widget — the **Texts half of the one "iPhone" widget** (`src/components/iphone-hub/IphoneWidget.tsx`, widget id `iphone`), shared with iPhone Notes; also a Home Screen web app ("Texts")

> Your texts, answered in your voice — you approve every reply

An iPhone Shortcut automation sends each incoming text here, and Jarvis drafts a reply in your voice — your own words
about how you text, plus every reply you rewrite. Nothing is sent until you approve it. Approve on the iPhone and it
sends at once through your own Messages app; approve on a computer and your phone buzzes so one tap sends it.

![Text Inbox](../../public/look/text-inbox.jpg)

## Features — every one of these must still exist after your change

The owner asked for each of these. Removing, hiding or "simplifying away" one is a regression,
even if the code looked unused. If a change needs one gone, ask first.

**The iPhone widget (shared with iPhone Notes)**
- **Texts half of the iPhone card** — count of texts to approve, the two newest (avatar initial, sender, text, "writing a reply…" / "reply ready to approve"); tapping it opens the sheet on Texts. `src/components/iphone-hub/IphoneWidget.tsx`
- **"Send N approved texts" button** on the card when on an iPhone with replies ready. `src/components/iphone-hub/IphoneWidget.tsx`
- **Sheet with a Notes / Texts switch** mounting `TextInboxApp embedded`. `src/components/iphone-hub/IphoneWidget.tsx` (`IphoneExpanded`)

- **AI draft in your voice** — uses your "How you text" line plus the replies you rewrote (style examples); a short safe starter when there is no key, the daily cap is spent or the call fails. `src/lib/text-inbox/server/brain.ts`, `src/lib/text-inbox/engine.ts` (`systemPrompt`)
- **Learns from rewrites** — every reply you edit before approving becomes a style example ("it also learns from every reply you rewrite (N so far)"). `src/lib/text-inbox/engine.ts`, `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxSetup.tsx`
- **Skips codes and alerts** — one-time codes, 5–6 digit short codes, spam/ads go straight to declined ("Skipped — looks automated") with no AI draft or notification; a question is never treated as automated. `src/lib/text-inbox/engine.ts`
- **No duplicates** — the same incoming text is deduped. `src/lib/text-inbox/engine.ts`
- **Status flow** drafting → waiting → ready → sent / declined; "typing" dots while drafting. `src/lib/text-inbox/engine.ts`, `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx`

**Approving (tabs: To approve · Ready to send · Sent · Set up)**
- **Conversation strip per text** — their grey bubble on the left, your draft as an editable bubble on the right, one action bar. `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx` (`Draft`)
- **Approve** (on iPhone: **Approve & send**) — on the iPhone it opens the "Jarvis Send" Shortcut (`shortcuts://x-callback-url/run-shortcut?name=Jarvis%20Send`, returns to the page); on a computer it moves the reply to Ready and pushes "Reply ready — tap to send" to the phone. `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx`, `src/lib/text-inbox/client.ts` (`sendFromPhone`, `onIphone`), `src/lib/text-inbox/engine.ts`

- **Decline** any draft. `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx`
- **Ready to send** — on the iPhone "Send N now"; on a computer a tip plus **Buzz my phone again**; **Undo** puts a reply back in To approve. `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx`
- **Banner** when replies are ready and you're on another tab ("Send N approved replies now" / "N approved — waiting for your phone"). `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx`
- **Opened from the notification** (`?send=1`) with replies waiting → hands them to the phone at once. `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx`
- **Sent tab** — sent and declined texts, **Send again**, **Remove**. `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx`
- **Summary meter** — to approve / ready / sent counts, "phone checked in x ago". `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx`
- **Try it with a pretend text** — From + Message → "Draft a reply", for when nothing is linked yet. `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxApp.tsx`

- **Part 2 · "Jarvis Send"** Shortcut — exact taps, no Key box needed. `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxSetup.tsx`

- **Notification switches** — "Buzz me when a new text has a draft ready", "Buzz my phone when I approve on the computer". `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxSetup.tsx`
- **How you text** — one line of tone, saved for every new draft. `src/components/text-inbox/TextInboxSetup.tsx`

# Trading Studio

`/apps/trading-studio` · Utilities · live · shows as: App plugins card (Jarvis › App plugins; it is in `PLUGIN_SLUGS` in `src/lib/studio/plugins.ts`, so it is **not** a hub tile). It is the home that EA World, EA Lab, EA Feature List and Multi-Order Calculator are merged into (`MERGED_INTO` in the same file).

> Every trading-bot tool, one front door

Every trading-bot tool behind one switcher, the way Jarvis Audio Studio holds its three studios. Each section is
still the app it used to be and has its own accent colour. The owner uses it to replay a bot against a real past
New York session, test bots on the PC, argue with a trade idea, open the outside market terminals, copy an EA
spec into a build, and price a basket of gold orders.

![Trading Studio](../../public/look/trading-studio.jpg)

## Features — every one of these must still exist after your change

The owner asked for each of these. Removing, hiding or "simplifying away" one is a regression,
even if the code looked unused. If a change needs one gone, ask first.

**The shell (one front door)**

- **Seven sections, in this order** — EA World · EA Lab · Trading Agent · Replay · Terminals · Feature List · Calculator, each with a label, hint, icon and accent hue (45, 150, 320, 205, 175, 265, 20). `src/lib/studio-home/trading.ts` (`TRADING_SECTIONS`)
- **Sliding-thumb switcher** — a tab bar whose highlight slides to the open section and scrolls sideways on a phone; the whole home's glow changes to the section's hue. `src/components/studio-home/StudioHome.tsx`, `src/components/studio-home/studio-home.css`
- **`?section=` in the address and last section remembered** — the address updates with `history.replaceState`; with no `?section=` it reopens the last section used on this device (localStorage key `trading-studio:section`); a first visit lands on Replay. `StudioHome.tsx`, `src/app/apps/trading-studio/page.tsx`, `trading.ts` (`TRADING_DEFAULT`, `TRADING_REMEMBER`)
- **One section's code at a time** — each section is loaded only when opened (Replay's chart library is never downloaded by someone checking a basket), with a skeleton while it loads. `src/components/trading-studio/TradingStudio.tsx` (`COMPONENTS`)
- **"On your PC" panel for EA World** — a plain-English panel saying EA World isn't on the website yet, with one button, "Ask Claude Code to bring it in", that files an In Queue request in folder `app:trading-studio`. `trading.ts` (`pending`), `StudioHome.tsx` (`PendingSection`), `src/lib/studio-home/fileRequest.ts`
- **Old links land in the right section** — `/apps/ea-feature-list` → Feature List, `/apps/multi-order-calculator` → Calculator, `/apps/ea-world/replay` → Replay, `/apps/ea-world/terminals` → Terminals, `/apps/ea-lab` → EA Lab (redirect pages); `/apps/ea-world` and `/apps/ea-lab` also redirect from `next.config.mjs` `redirects()`. `src/app/apps/{ea-feature-list,multi-order-calculator,ea-lab}/page.tsx`, `src/app/apps/ea-world/{replay,terminals}/page.tsx`, `next.config.mjs`

**EA Lab section** — full detail in [ea-lab.md](ea-lab.md)

- **The testing bench, mounted embedded** — no wordmark of its own inside the studio, but it keeps the runner status and its buttons. `src/components/ea-lab/EaLab.tsx` (`embedded`)

**Trading Agent section**

- **"Reads setups. Places nothing." banner** — always at the top, even embedded (the component has no `embedded` prop on purpose): no broker connection, no order path. `src/components/trading-agent/TradingAgent.tsx`
- **The setup form** — instrument, long/short, timeframe, entry, stop, target, account size and risk per trade %. `TradingAgent.tsx`
- **The arithmetic, computed in the browser** — risk and reward per unit, reward:risk, breakeven win rate, position size, and expectancy at assumed win rates 30–70 %; works with no key and no network. `src/lib/trading-agent/setup.ts` (`numbersFor`, `expectancy`), `TradingAgent.tsx` (`WIN_RATES`)
- **Flaw checks** — warns when prices don't agree with each other (e.g. entry equals stop) before anything is asked. `setup.ts` (`flawsIn`)
- **"Read it back to me"** — a model restates the bet without the reasons, then lists What it assumes · What would kill it before your stop does · Where the argument is weakest · What you did not say. It is handed the figures already computed and never asked to do sums. `TradingAgent.tsx`, `src/app/api/trading-agent/read/route.ts`, `src/lib/trading-agent/prompt.ts`
- **Three refusals** — no verdict on taking the trade, no price/probability forecast, no mention of orders, brokers or platforms. `src/lib/trading-agent/prompt.ts` (`readSystem`)
- **No-key fallback** — with no AI key the route answers `offline` and the left-side numbers still work. `src/app/api/trading-agent/read/route.ts` (`aiConfigured`)

**Replay section**

- **Real past ticks** — pick a symbol (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, AUD/USD, USD/JPY, Gold, US30, NAS100, S&P 500, Bitcoin), a New York day (or an older one by date), and a window, then Load tape; real Dukascopy bid **and** ask, fetched hour by hour, with missing hours listed. `src/components/ea-replay/ReplayStudio.tsx`, `src/lib/ea-replay/instruments.ts`, `src/app/api/ea-replay/ticks/route.ts`, `src/lib/ea-replay/dukascopy.ts`
- **Session windows** — NY peak 08:00–11:00, NY open 09:30–11:30, London/NY overlap, Data drop 08:25–09:00, NY full, or Custom HHMM. `src/lib/ea-replay/session.ts` (`SESSION_PRESETS`)
- **Simulated MT4 broker** — balance, leverage, round-turn commission, latency, stop slippage, stop level, margin with a 50 % stop-out; all editable in the Broker panel. `src/lib/ea-replay/broker.ts`, `ReplayStudio.tsx`
- **Playback** — restart, play/pause, one tick, jump to next fill; speeds 1x, 5x, 20x, 60x, 300x and max; a scrubber (seeking back replays from the start so the result is exact); keyboard Space / → / Shift+→. `ReplayStudio.tsx` (`SPEEDS`, key handler)
- **Chart with the bot's orders on it** — TradingView lightweight-charts candles (5s / 15s / 1m / 5m), gray tape with the bot's buy/sell orders in colour, HUD, legend, follow button. `src/components/ea-replay/chartController.ts`, `ReplayStudio.tsx` (`TIMEFRAMES`)
- **Account panel** — equity, balance, closed trades, win rate, max drawdown, and an equity sparkline. `ReplayStudio.tsx`
- **Ledgers** — tabs Trades (click a row to replay from just before that entry) · Working · Events · Stats (profit factor, expectancy, average spread…) · Bot log. `ReplayStudio.tsx`, `src/lib/ea-replay/stats.ts`
- **Built-in bots** — HFT Secret v2 (wave + HFT, the default), HFT Secret (rebuild), NY Opening Range Breakout, each with grouped editable inputs remembered per pair; 45-minute warm-up so v2's 34-SMA channel is formed. `src/lib/ea-replay/strategies/{index,hftSecretV2,hftSecret,openingRange}.ts`, `ReplayStudio.tsx` (`WARMUP_MS`)
- **The EA sources to download** — `HFT_Secret_Rebuild.mq4` (v1) and `HFT_Secret_v2.mq4` (v2: 34-SMA high/low wave + HFT, breakeven, flatten at session end, daily target, distances in price), twins of the replay bots. `public/ea-world/experts/`
- **Bring a bot** — drop or paste an `.mq4` and "Port with AI" (the model lists what it could not carry over), or write one by hand from a template; code is shown and checked before it can be saved; an `.ex4` is refused with the reason. `src/components/ea-replay/BotBench.tsx`, `src/app/api/ea-replay/port/route.ts`, `src/lib/ea-replay/{custom,portPrompt}.ts`
- **Fingerprint the original** — drop an MT4 statement or Strategy Tester report; it measures stop, target, trail step, pending-order use, lots, side and NY hours, then applies them to HFT Secret v2 with the reason for each. `src/components/ea-replay/FingerprintPanel.tsx`, `src/lib/ea-replay/statement.ts`
- **Your own ticks / demo tape** — load a Dukascopy, MT5 or plain time,bid,ask CSV (with an MT5 server-offset box), or a Demo tape; the same offers appear when a window has no tape. `ReplayStudio.tsx` (`TapeFallbacks`), `src/lib/ea-replay/{csv,demo}.ts`

**Terminals section**

- **Three outside terminals in one table** — OpenTerminal (localhost:3400), Vibe-Trading (localhost:8899), Fincept Terminal (desktop app), each with what it adds, what it needs and a live up/down check (Check again). `src/components/ea-replay/TerminalsStudio.tsx`, `src/lib/ea-replay/terminals.ts`
- **Start and open them** — "Copy start command" for PowerShell, "Open in a tab", and "Show here" (OpenTerminal framed inside the page); an Open Replay link. `TerminalsStudio.tsx`
- **PC install/start scripts** — install once, start every time; installs to `%USERPROFILE%\Projects\ea-terminals`, outside the repo. `tools/ea-terminals/{install.ps1,start.ps1,README.md}`

**Feature List section**

- **Every dictated EA spec** — searchable (title, tags, spec text) with tag chips that combine, a count, and a row per spec. `src/components/ea/EaFeatureList.tsx`, `src/components/ea/EaFeatureRow.tsx`, `src/lib/ea-features/features.ts` (`filterFeatures`, `allTags`)
- **Spec window with Copy spec** — the full verbatim spec, one click to the clipboard, with the date it was added. `src/components/ea/EaFeatureDetailModal.tsx`
- **Specs live in code** — added by appending to `EA_FEATURES`, so they ship on every device with no database. `src/lib/ea-features/features.ts`

**Calculator section**

- **Basket of orders** — buy/sell rows with lots and entry; add, duplicate, delete; per-order P/L. `src/components/calculator/Calculator.tsx`, `src/components/calculator/OrderRow.tsx`
- **Two modes** — Target exit → P/L, or Desired profit → the exit price that makes it. `Calculator.tsx` (`Mode`), `src/lib/calculator/engine.ts` (`solveExitPriceForPnl`)
- **Basket settings** — target exit, current price, spread, commission/lot, swap/lot, account currency; symbol XAUUSD (100 oz/lot). `Calculator.tsx`, `src/lib/calculator/symbols.ts`
- **Profit curve** — P/L across prices with Break-even, Target and Current-price markers and a hover crosshair tooltip. `src/components/calculator/ProfitChart.tsx`
- **Results** — gross P/L, commission, swap, spread cost, total and net lots, weighted average entry, break-even price, $ per point / pip, distance to target. `Calculator.tsx`, `engine.ts` (`evaluateBasket`)
- **Saved baskets** — save, load, rename, duplicate, delete; synced to every device. `Calculator.tsx`, `src/lib/calculator/storage.ts`
- **Export** — CSV and JSON downloads. `storage.ts` (`ordersToCsv`, `downloadFile`)

## How it looks

- **Look:** the shared Studio home shell (generalised from Jarvis Audio Studio); no `.impeccable` record for this app. Each section keeps its own original look.
- **Colours / type:** DESIGN.md tokens (`#0a0b0f` canvas, `#12141c` panel, `#e9ecf3` ink, system sans, JetBrains Mono for numbers). Accent is a hue, not a colour: `--sh-accent: oklch(0.74 0.15 var(--sh-hue))`, per section. Replay's own rule: "the tape is gray, the bot is in colour" — buy `#3b82f6`, sell `#f59e0b`, win `#22c55e`, loss `#f87171`, playhead `#e3bb4f` (`src/components/ea-replay/replay.css`). Calculator chart: target `#6366f1`, now `#f59e0b`, break-even `#9aa3b5`. Trading Agent: amber lock, emerald/rose expectancy.
- **Layout:** laptop — one bar (brand, switcher) over a full-height stage; Replay is a top strip, chart + right rail, ledgers at the bottom; Agent is a 420px arithmetic column + reasoning pane; Calculator is 2/3 orders + chart, 1/3 results. Phone — the switcher wraps to its own full-width row and scrolls sideways (≤900px), hints and the brand subtitle drop (≤560px); Replay stacks with a 56vh chart (≤900px); Agent and Calculator stack to one column.
- **Signature pieces:** the sliding-thumb switcher with hue glow, Replay's gray-tape chart with coloured orders, the "Reads setups. Places nothing." banner.
- **Motion:** the hue glides (520ms) and the glow slides when switching; stage fades in. `prefers-reduced-motion` turns off shell transitions and the stage animation (`studio-home.css`) and Replay transitions (`replay.css`).

## Where the code is

| Part | Path |
|---|---|
| Page | `src/app/apps/trading-studio/page.tsx` |
| UI | `src/components/trading-studio/` (shell) · `src/components/studio-home/` · `src/components/ea-lab/` · `src/components/trading-agent/` · `src/components/ea-replay/` (Replay + Terminals) · `src/components/ea/` (Feature List) · `src/components/calculator/` |
| Logic + tests | `src/lib/studio-home/trading.ts` (+ `sections.test.ts`) · `src/lib/ea-lab/` · `src/lib/trading-agent/` · `src/lib/ea-replay/` · `src/lib/ea-features/` · `src/lib/calculator/` |
| API | `src/app/api/trading-agent/read/` · `src/app/api/ea-replay/{ticks,port}/` |
| PC helpers | `tools/ea-terminals/` (outside terminals) · `tools/ea-lab-runner/` (EA Lab runner) |
| Saved data | synced keys `ea-replay:bots` (your bots), `moc:scenarios:v1` (saved baskets); localStorage only: `ea-replay:prefs`, `trading-studio:section`. EA Lab's records live on the runner's PC (`C:\EA-Lab`) |

## Owner's rules for this app

- **Never create `src/app/apps/ea-world/page.tsx` from a cloud session.** EA World's code is only on the owner's PC (uncommitted). `/apps/ea-world` redirects in from `next.config.mjs`, not from a file. The same rule was set for `src/app/apps/ea-lab/`; EA Lab has since been brought in (commit 30052bb) and its `page.tsx` is now a committed redirect — still do not add anything else there.
- Wiring EA World in is one edit in `TradingStudio.tsx` (the comment gives the exact `dynamic(() => import("../ea-world/EaWorld")…)` line) plus deleting `pending` on `world` in `trading.ts` — and only with the PC's code committed.
- A section is either pending or mounted, never both.
- The Trading Agent has no order path and no broker connection, by design; it is named `trading-agent`, never `money-agent` (that is Money Agent Studio).
- Every section mounts with `embedded`; each still works standalone at its old look.
- In Queue folder for this app: `app:trading-studio`.

## Described but not found in code

- The catalog overview says "Six trading tools" and that EA Lab runs only on the PC "once its code is brought onto the website"; the code has seven sections and EA Lab is mounted (stale text in `src/lib/catalog.ts` and CLAUDE.md's "Where things live" row, which still calls `lab` pending).
- EA World itself (Analyze · Vault · Bench) — described in `src/lib/catalog.ts`; only the pending panel exists here. See [ea-world.md](ea-world.md).
